title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' block, the Grothendieck–Teichmüller/'loop equation' part that continues La Longue Marche. The group 𝔊 carries a filtration 𝔊 ⊃ 𝔊^+ ⊃ Π ⊃ Π_0 with graded pieces 𝔊/𝔊^+ ≃ μ (order 2), 𝔊^+/Π ≃ 𝔖_3 and Π/Π_0 ≃ μ. So 𝔊/Π_0 is a finite group of order 24. The previous page relates it to quotients of GL(2,Ẑ) and to (Z/4Z)^*. The group M (a group of 'automorphisms' or solutions of the loop equation) has an analogous filtration M ⊃ M'' ⊃ M''^! ⊃ M^{0!}. It carries characters ε_2 : M → μ and ε_3 : M''^! → μ, and a canonical homomorphism (45) M → 𝔊/Π_0. The goal, carried into the next page, is to compute the kernel of N_ρ^* → 𝔊/Π_0, where N_ρ^* is a normalizer-type subgroup attached to ρ, D_ρ a (dihedral/decomposition-type) subgroup and M^0(−j) a twisted subgroup. One wants this kernel to be exactly M^0(−j), giving the injective homomorphism '(4σ)'.

Argument on this page.
(1) A certain subgroup M''^!_α (probably M''^!_0) maps into the centre of 𝔊/Π_0.
(2) That centre lies in 𝔊^+/Π_0 and equals μ = image of Π/Π_0. The reason given: a central element of 𝔊^+/Π_0 maps to a central element of 𝔊^+/Π ≃ 𝔖_3, whose centre is trivial. Conversely Π/Π_0 has order 2 and is normal, hence central.
(3) This gives a factorisation M''^! → μ ↪ Z(𝔊/Π_0). One must check that this map is ε_3, hence trivial on M^{0!} and a fortiori on M^0(0). G. notes in the text and margin that this is not yet verified ('on y reviendra plus bas').
(4) A crossed-out continuation: assuming the point, N_ρ^* → 𝔊/Π_0 factors through (*) N_ρ^*/M^0(−j) → 𝔊/Π_0. The composite D_ρ ↪ N_ρ^*/M^0(−j) → 𝔊/Π_0 is injective, so ker(*) is a normal subgroup meeting D_ρ trivially. Since D_ρ has index 2, the kernel has order 1 or 2.

G. abandons this case analysis ('Je vois mieux'). On the next page he replaces it by a cleaner Proposition: M → 𝔊/Π_0 respects the two three-step filtrations and induces the evident isomorphisms on graded pieces (via ε_2, the 𝔖_3 piece, ε_3). Hence its kernel is M^{0!}, and the desired kernel is M'(−J) ∩ M'' = M^0(−J).
errors: Step (2) asserts without proof that Z(𝔊/Π_0) ⊂ 𝔊^+/Π_0. The 𝔖_3 argument only controls central elements already lying in 𝔊^+/Π_0. One needs that no element outside 𝔊^+/Π_0 is central, which depends on the precise extension structure; this is plausible but unchecked on the page.
The identification of the induced map M''^! → μ with ε_3 is explicitly left unverified. G. himself flags the issue with M''^!_0 in the margin and abandons the crossed-out route.
The crossed-out argument as written only yields |ker| ≤ 2, not triviality. That is why it was abandoned in favour of the graded-isomorphism Proposition on the next page.

ideas.what: Centre of the order-24 quotient 𝔊/Π_0 equals the order-2 subgroup Π/Π_0, deduced from Z(𝔖_3) = 1
ideas.modern_name: elementary finite group theory (centre of a central extension of S_3)

ideas.what: Comparison of compatible filtrations on M (via characters ε_2, ε_3) and on 𝔊/Π_0 to compute the kernel of M → 𝔊/Π_0
ideas.modern_name: graded comparison / five-lemma style argument for filtered groups; mod-level-2/4 reduction in Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard technique; GT context: Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Ambient themes appear in Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche, but not this specific computation

ideas.what: Normal subgroup meeting an index-2 subgroup D_ρ trivially has order ≤ 2

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine working page: an elementary centre computation in an order-24 finite quotient, plus an abandoned kernel argument that G. replaces on the next page. It is technical scaffolding inside the loop-equation notes, with no new result or connection on the page itself.
transcription_corrections: 'M''!_α' is more likely M''^!_0 (a subscript 0 written hastily); compare the margin 'mais M''^!_0'.
'En fait on a vu [?] ainsi que Ker(ε_3|M''!)' is probably 'En fait on n'a vu que Ker(ε_3 | M''^!) ... (qui contient ...)', i.e. only a containment has been established.
Margin: 'mais M''^!_0 — ... μ ! — on y reviendra plus bas'; the middle part is partly illegible.
The diagonal strokes cross out the whole passage from 'Admettons provisoirement ce point' to the end of the page.
